summary: Burundi requires most visitors to obtain a visa in advance through the migration authority's official online portal, with tourist visas typically issued for stays of up to 30 days, while fellow East African Community citizens receive a free EAC visa of up to six months at any point of entry.

notes: Plastic bags are banned in Burundi — repack your luggage into paper, cloth or reusable bags before arrival, as bags can be confiscated at the border.

payments.text: Burundi is a cash economy. Cards work only at a handful of hotels in Bujumbura and ATMs rarely accept foreign cards. Bring your budget in cash (US dollars or euros; large, recent US notes get the best rates) and exchange through banks or licensed bureaux.

safety.text: Several foreign governments advise reconsidering travel to Burundi because of political tension, crime and sporadic armed incidents, particularly in areas bordering the DR Congo. Bujumbura and the main tourist spots are usually calm, but avoid demonstrations, travel by day and check current advisories before you go.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The long dry season from June to September is the most comfortable time for Lake Tanganyika's beaches, Kibira National Park and travel on unpaved roads.

tips.text: Check your government's travel advisory shortly before departure. The security situation can change quickly, and areas near the DR Congo border in particular should be avoided.
Plastic bags are illegal in Burundi and can be confiscated on arrival — pack with cloth or paper bags instead.
Bring clean, recent US dollar notes for your whole budget. Cards and international ATMs are unreliable, and older or marked bills are often refused.
Do not photograph government buildings, military sites, airports or officials. It can lead to questioning or detention.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Burundi?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. Apply for an eVisa through the migration authority's official portal (migration.gov.bi) before travel — tourist visas are typically issued for 30 days. Citizens of East African Community countries such as Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and Rwanda get a free EAC visa at the border instead.

faq.question: Which passports get a free visa at the border?
faq.answer: Citizens of the East African Community partner states — Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, South Sudan, the DR Congo and Somalia — need no visa in advance: the migration authority grants them a free 'EAC visa' at any point of entry, for stays of up to six months. It does not allow work.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Burundi?
faq.answer: Do not count on it. Burundi has moved visa issuance online, and travelers are expected to arrive with an eVisa approval obtained through the official portal. Apply in advance and carry a printed copy.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Burundi?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK and Canadian travel advice both say a yellow fever vaccination certificate is required to enter Burundi, whichever country you arrive from. Carry the yellow card with your passport.

faq.question: Is Burundi safe to visit?
faq.answer: Bujumbura, Lake Tanganyika's shore and the main sights are usually calm, but several governments advise reconsidering travel because of political tension, crime and incidents near the DR Congo border. Travel by day, avoid gatherings, and check current advisories before and during your trip.
